statutoryBasis: Health Products Act 2007 (Cap. 122D); Health Products (Therapeutic Products) Regulations 2016 Part 6 (Duties of Registrants); HSA Guidance on Post-Marketing Vigilance
provenance: Health Sciences Authority (HSA) Vigilance and Compliance Branch (VCB); WHO Collaborating Centre for International Drug Monitoring (WHO-UMC)

authority.name: Health Sciences Authority (HSA)
authority.system: HSA PRISM Adverse Event Reporting Portal

SERIOUS_FATAL_OR_LIFE_THREATENING.description: Serious adverse reactions causing death or immediately life-threatening must be reported to HSA VCB within 15 calendar days of receipt

SERIOUS_OTHER.description: Other serious adverse reactions (inpatient hospitalisation, significant disability/incapacity, birth defect) must be reported within 15 calendar days

NON_SERIOUS.description: Non-serious adverse events must be tabulated and submitted in Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Reports (PBRER / PSUR)

causalityLevels.description: Event or laboratory test abnormality, with plausible time relationship to drug intake; cannot be explained by disease or other drugs; response to dechallenge plausible; rechallenge satisfactory.
Event with reasonable time sequence to administration of drug; unlikely attributed to concurrent disease; clinically reasonable response on dechallenge; rechallenge not required.
Event with reasonable time sequence to administration; could also be explained by concurrent disease or other drugs; information on dechallenge may be lacking or unclear.
Event with a temporal relationship to drug administration which makes a causal connection improbable, and other drugs or underlying disease provide plausible explanations.
Event or laboratory test abnormality reported as an adverse reaction, about which more data is essential for a proper assessment.
A report suggesting an adverse reaction which cannot be judged because information is insufficient or contradictory, and which cannot be supplemented or verified.
